run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 14 of the usual 15 holdings. ASML Holding wasn't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the company itself.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up a touch, but the real story is that it's fallen about 31% from its high — unusually cheap for a defense contractor whose order backlog keeps steadily building, with military spending still on its side.

ASML.sentence: ASML Holding didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

LIN.sentence: Linde is edging up while the broader market sells off — when investors get nervous they tend to park money in steady businesses like industrial gas, and this is about as steady as it gets.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft drifted down a touch and sits about 12% off its high, but there's no drama here — the AI cloud story keeps grinding along steadily in the background.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped slightly and is sitting near its highs again, so there's nothing dramatic here — just the steady lab-equipment supplier that sells to pretty much every biotech and research lab out there.

CVX.sentence: Chevron rose a bit as oil stays elevated because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments — just remember those fat profits are the war-time oil price, not the company getting better, and its ordinary planning price is much lower.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen hard — nearly cut in half from its high — even though big companies and government agencies keep signing multi-year contracts for its workflow-automation and AI-assistant tools, so the price drop looks out of step with how the business is actually doing.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore rose in step with copper prices, which is exactly what you'd expect from a company that both mines copper and runs the world's largest commodity-trading desk — nothing unusual going on.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta climbed again, and the part that matters is that the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still rising faster than its costs — the quarry-owns-its-own-territory advantage is fully intact.

KOF.sentence: The Mexican Coca-Cola bottler edged up, but a weakening peso is a headwind since most of its earnings are in pesos and worth less when converted back to dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber had a strong day, and the number that counts keeps looking healthy — people are booking roughly 20% more rides than a year ago, so the core business is clearly still growing fast.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is quietly steady, and the shipping giant is priced below what its own fleet of ships would cost to replace, which gives it a solid floor underneath.

MA.sentence: Mastercard had a good day, and its price premium over Visa has shrunk to almost nothing — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so there's no sign of anything actually wrong with the business.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot company slipped a bit and is down almost 30% from its high, yet hospitals still plan to do 13–15% more procedures with its machines next year — a gap between the fear and the actual evidence.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell about 4% along with the other AI names after Google's parent and Amazon showed they're now borrowing to pay for all the computing gear they buy — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
